content.user_title: Connect your app to Caveman measurement
content.value_statement: LLM requests can be difficult to measure across SDKs and providers. This skill identifies live callsites, routes them through Caveman, and verifies one measured request.
actual_capabilities: Finds common LLM SDK imports, raw provider HTTP calls, and base-URL environment variables.
Lists discovered LLM callsites before making repository changes.
Provides routing patterns for OpenAI, Anthropic, Vercel AI SDK, LangChain, LangGraph, LiteLLM, and raw HTTP.
Adds Caveman gateway configuration through environment variables instead of source literals.
Explains stored-key and bring-your-own-key gateway modes.
Verifies a configured integration with one small provider request and reports the observed result.
limitations: The skill only covers LLM providers and frameworks described in its instructions.
It requires a valid Caveman gateway URL and API key supplied by the user.
Verification makes a real, billable provider request.
It does not validate Caveman Cloud security, availability, or privacy practices.

use_cases.title: Measure a production AI service
use_cases.description: Route existing application LLM traffic through the gateway to capture request usage and spend.

use_cases.title: Standardize SDK gateway routing
use_cases.description: Apply documented gateway configuration to OpenAI, Anthropic, or framework-based LLM clients.

use_cases.title: Verify observability onboarding
use_cases.description: Send one minimal request and confirm that the gateway records usage before wider rollout.

prompt_templates.title: Set up basic measurement
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up Caveman measurement for this repository. First identify all live LLM callsites and show me the planned changes.

prompt_templates.title: Configure an OpenAI client
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure the existing OpenAI SDK client to use the Caveman gateway. Use environment variables and preserve current provider behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review gateway changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this repository for LLM callsites and propose the minimal Caveman gateway integration. Do not make unrelated changes.

prompt_templates.title: Verify controlled rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: After configuring Caveman, show the exact verification request and wait for my approval before sending any billable traffic.

output_examples.input: Set up measurement for the repository.
output: Found two LLM callsites in the API service.
Added gateway URL and gateway key references through the existing environment configuration.
Verification is ready and requires approval before sending a provider request.

output_examples.input: Check whether the gateway integration succeeded.
output: The response included usage details for the configured model.
Record mode is enabled and no optimization was configured.

best_practices: Review the proposed file changes before applying them.
Store gateway and provider credentials only in ignored environment files or a managed secret store.
Confirm the target gateway and approve the billable verification request before it runs.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode gateway or provider credentials in application source.
Do not route traffic to an unverified gateway URL.
Do not report successful measurement without an observed verification result.

faq.question: What does this skill configure?
faq.answer: It routes supported LLM client traffic through the Caveman gateway for usage and spend measurement.

faq.question: Does it change model output?
faq.answer: The skill describes record-mode routing intended to preserve request behavior, but you should verify this in your environment.

faq.question: Which client libraries are covered?
faq.answer: It includes patterns for OpenAI, Anthropic, Vercel AI SDK, LangChain, LangGraph, LiteLLM, and raw HTTP.

faq.question: Are credentials required?
faq.answer: Yes. A Caveman API key is required, and bring-your-own-key mode may send an existing provider key to the gateway.

faq.question: Does verification cost money?
faq.answer: Yes. Verification sends one real provider request and can create provider charges.

faq.question: Should I approve network activity first?
faq.answer: Yes. Confirm the gateway URL, credential handling, and verification request before allowing network activity.
